chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Recording with Billie Holiday, Prez and Una Mae Carlisle
summary: Collins names players he recorded with, including a late-night date with Billie and Lester Young and Victor sides with Una Mae Carlisle that were never promoted.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let's see, Bill Doggett, Billie Holiday, Roy, Don -- Redman, Art, just to name a few. It's just-- you know, it was -- I was playing with Roy, and at the -- I think it was the -- it was Kelly's Stables and we recorded with -- Billie wanted us to record with her so we recorded after we got off that night. And I think the piano player was Eddie Heywood, Prez, it was just some good, you know -- it was just -- everything was so spontaneous, and I made some good records with Prez during that time with a singer by the name of Una Mae Carlyle. You probably -- do you re-

member her? Yeah. Well, we did some very good recordings for her, but unfortunately they were for Victor who -- that was the burial ground. You know, Victor recorded more good artists and never distributed the records at all. I don't understand it.
